version.changelog:
- Documentation updated to clarify that OpenClaw config is now read via environment variables (e.g., DEEPSEEK_API_KEY), not just the JSON config file.
- No code changes in this release.

llm.summary: This skill mostly does what it says, but its AI mode can automatically send scripts and API credentials to environment-selected endpoints without enough disclosure or control.

dimensions.detail: Using LLM API keys is purpose-aligned, but inherited environment variables control both credentials and request destinations. The code does not restrict destinations to official HTTPS provider hosts or require confirmation for custom gateways.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install step is non-silent and only runs setup.sh, which chmods the bundled runner script. There are no package installs, downloads, or hidden setup actions observed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The English-only report format and promotional footer are disclosed in the skill text, but the footer is mandatory and unrelated to the requested analysis. The documentation also does not clearly warn that script contents may leave the machine in AI mode.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background worker, startup hook, or filesystem write was found beyond chmod during setup. The skill reads only the user-selected script file at runtime, but the test command logs the first 10 characters of the configured API key.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The script analyzer purpose is coherent, but AI mode sends the full user script to external LLM APIs when provider credentials are present, and custom *_BASE_URL environment variables can redirect credential-bearing requests without validation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if your scripts are private or your LLM API keys are valuable. Use it only in an environment where provider base URL variables are trusted, avoid running the connection test in shared logs, and assume AI mode may send the complete script to the configured external provider. Local fallback behavior appears non-persistent and non-destructive.
llm.findings:
[PE3] unexpected: Downgraded: the referenced .env text says no .env file is needed; the code reads API keys from environment variables and does not load credential files.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted as a material disclosure concern: AI analysis is purpose-aligned, but the full script is sent to external providers automatically when credentials exist, without a clear runtime warning or local-only control.
[RA2] unexpected: Downgraded: the artifact mentions creating ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json as user setup guidance, but the inspected runtime code does not create persistence, cron jobs, startup scripts, or state files.
[SDI-4] expected: Partially accepted as a documentation mismatch: the internal comment says no filesystem access for config, while the CLI intentionally reads the user-specified script file. This is expected for CLI analysis and not hidden broad file access.
[E1] expected: External LLM calls are expected for AI-backed script analysis, but they remain sensitive because script content and API credentials are transmitted.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: English output is explicitly branded and documented as the English edition, so this is not a security concern by itself.
[T01] unexpected: Partially accepted: the mandatory promotional footer is disclosed in SKILL.md and present in both AI and local output paths, so it is not hidden instruction hijacking, but users should know it cannot be disabled.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: the code permits unvalidated custom provider base URLs and attaches API credentials to those requests; the test command also prints an API key prefix.
